start_here: Say to your AI: "Read my record note:abc". It calls tool:your-records at @tools with tools:run and {call: {name: "records:read", arguments: {id: "abc", type: "note"}}}; the engine starts the person's records session on the first call and every later call reaches the same one. A run of any other tool reaches the same records through the engine's records door (tools/records-door), which sends the call here.
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it keeps every record you have, whatever its list or kind, as rows in your own database.
instructions: 1. Make sure your database connection (own-rows-postgres-connection) is saved in your vault; the engine mounts it on descriptor 8 and never prints it. A person with no database sets settings.json `store` to a SQLite file instead.

2. Ask your AI for your records. Each ask is one call: tools:run at @tools with {tool: "tool:your-records", call: {name, arguments}}, where name is an operation of mcp-tools.json (records:read, records:list, records:search, records:write, records:result, workspace:read, workspace:write).
3. A write names every record's id and type, and the same request key sent again answers the first receipt and changes nothing.
4. An answer too big for one message comes as a byte page: send the same call again with after_byte set to the page's next_after_byte until it is null.

worked_examples.title: Read a record
worked_examples.hands_back: {tool: "tool:your-records", result: {structuredContent: {id, type, value}}}: value is null when there is no such record.

worked_examples.title: List the newest records of a kind
worked_examples.hands_back: {records: [{id, type, value}], next}: greatest id first; next is null at the end.

worked_examples.title: Search my records
worked_examples.ask: Find the notes about a red boat
worked_examples.hands_back: {question, terms, results: [{id, type, title, said, score, address}]}: each address is the read that opens the record.
